newsitem.title: FRANCE: French would reject Maastricht, given second chance.
newsitem.headline: French would reject Maastricht, given second chance.

text.p: French people would vote "no" to the Maastricht Treaty, the European Union's blueprint for a single currency and closer political integration, if they got the chance in a new referendum, an opinion poll showed on Thursday.

The SOFRES survey for Pelerin Magazine found that 55 percent would probably reject the treaty and 45 percent vote in favour. In a 1992 referendum, French people voted 51-49 percent to endorse the treaty.
Yet the poll also found that just 44 percent of 800 people interviewed on January 30 and February 1 regretted that France had ratified the treaty in 1992 while 43 percent were satisfied.
The survey showed French people reckoned closer European union would clearly bolster defence, security and the fight against terrorism and help firms tackle international competition.
But they believed it would worsen French social welfare and slightly hamper employment in France.
Other polls have generally shown that the French people still favour taking part in the planned single currency from 1999.
